catalog.title: J-space analysis
catalog.mac: Research methods: Author request, review inputs, then open execution and evidence. Both CLIs use science interview/draft/publish and the same managed engine.
outputs: Operation report and its provenance; inspect the declared run/config output.
catalog.restriction: Explicit config, reviewed input hashes and a fresh engine plan are required. GPU work requires immutable model revisions. Outputs are new records; local/Slurm execution uses the existing scientific owner. Native MLX numerical equivalence is not claimed. Remote training and analysis outputs are retained; the diagnostic cleanup policy does not authorize their removal. The batch owner currently requires OptVec artifact layer/dose metadata; J-space remains a separate method.

actions.authorityReason: Inspect staged scientific inputs and execution resources without execution or authorship.
Execute a reviewed scientific operation and retain its scientific output type.

access.restriction: Calls the existing route with its existing service role and scientific gates. Request path parameters, query and body remain explicit; this adapter does not change execution topology or retry mutations.

interview.title: Analyze an intervention in J-space
interview.purpose: Inspect downstream residual changes through an imported J-lens. This does not optimize or train a vector.

interview.claimBoundary: Arithmetic fidelity, predictive readout and behavioral/causal evidence are different. This operation supplies no behavioral causal test; null draws are comparators, not calibrated p-values. The current batch implementation requires OptVec artifact metadata for layer and dose; other artifact types are not yet accepted.
questions: Which intervention, lens and probe distribution answer the question?
What observation layers and dose are justified?
What separate controlled behavioral study will test any causal interpretation?
